# Breadcrumb Specification

Every generated script, workflow, or configuration file created using the project toolkit must include a breadcrumb comment header on its first lines.

## Purpose

The origin breadcrumb records which toolkit revision and profile generated a file, providing traceability without requiring git submodules or permanent in-repo toolkit linkage.

## Format

Use the appropriate comment syntax for the file type:

### PowerShell scripts (`.ps1`, `.psm1`) and YAML workflows (`.yml`, `.yaml`)
```powershell
# Generated by project-toolkit
# Source: <toolkit-repo-url>
# Commit: <commit-sha>
# Profile: <profile-name>
# Generated: <ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-09-06T10:00:00Z>
```

### C# / C / C++ source files (`.cs`)
```csharp
// Generated by project-toolkit
// Source: <toolkit-repo-url>
// Commit: <commit-sha>
// Profile: <profile-name>
// Generated: <ISO 8601 UTC timestamp>
```

### Markdown / HTML files (`.md`, `.html`)
```html
<!--
Generated by project-toolkit
Source: <toolkit-repo-url>
Commit: <commit-sha>
Profile: <profile-name>
Generated: <ISO 8601 UTC timestamp>
-->
```

## Rules

1. Place the breadcrumb at the very top of the generated file before any function definitions or logic.
2. Replace `<toolkit-repo-url>`, `<commit-sha>`, `<profile-name>`, and `<ISO 8601 UTC timestamp>` with actual values resolved at bootstrap time.
3. Do not modify or remove breadcrumb headers during routine project maintenance.
